LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 15.3.1 IMPERATIVES (COMMANDS) INTERJECTIONS OF EXCITEMENT/JOY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.3: Language Use 15.3.1 Imperatives (commands) Interjections of excitement/joy
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 15.3.1 Imperatives (commands) Interjections of excitement/joy, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: What commands do we give to each other? 2.When do use interjections of excitement/joy?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 15.3.1 Imperatives (commands) Interjections of excitement/joy together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration -through pair/ group work.

• Creativity and imagination- during dialogues/ role play with peers.

Values:
Responsibility as learner responds to commands and interjection appropriately.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life Skills (effective communication) - as learner gains knowledge on appropriate use of commands and interjections

Link to other Learning Areas: Interjections and imperatives are learnt in Kiswahili and Indigenous Languages Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Audio recordings, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
